accessible_status_message_note: Important confirmation and failure messages remain available in accessible text and are exposed as meaningful status updates for assistive technology.
confirmation_visibility_note: The post-submit state remains reviewable on the destination page rather than depending only on a transient toast or auto-closing modal.
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes that accept a submission or important request keep the post-submit outcome, retained record, next-step timing, and safe-retry/help posture clear enough that the voter does not have to guess whether the action landed.
next_step_and_timing_note: The confirmation state says what happens next, what follow-up window or expected signal applies, and when the voter should switch to the ordinary help lane.
pending_vs_submitted_note: The route does not blur together fully submitted, saved/pending, and additional-action-needed states.
reference_identifier_note: When the route issues a case, reference, or receipt number, the confirmation state keeps it visible in accessible text rather than hiding it in a transient overlay.
retained_record_note: The voter can keep a bounded record of successful submission that includes what was submitted, where, and when, without exposing more personal data than necessary.
safe_retry_note: The route reduces duplicate-submission guesswork by making clear when retry is unnecessary, when retry is safe after visible failure, and when the voter should stop retrying and use help.
submission_confirmation_surface_label: Example State official voter-information submission-confirmation fail-open policy
submission_outcome_note: The route explicitly distinguishes ordinary post-submit states such as submitted, pending review, needs more action, and failed/not submitted when those differences matter.
